**O9a frozen contract — fixed native shell probe (40–41%):** add source-only `modules/lib/native_shell.sh`, exposing only `cfmgr_native_shell_probe ROOT`. This is an explicit fixed-probe exception for a trusted synchronous native-config-root callback; all general callback/payload restrictions remain. Require the live root-owner context (`root` mode, native-devices layout with extended configuration enabled, retained Opt ready, production or explicit fixture kind), exact owner ROOT/guard, active callback intent and FD6 directory identity. The caller already owns trusted immutable native code/ancestors, frozen root aliases, no inherited application FD above9, admitted FD8/FD9, aggregate group/deadline supervision and launch authority. These preconditions are not established by scalar flags or path checks alone. Never expose CLI/opkg/network execution or accept arbitrary command/script arguments.

Before launch, reject loader cache/preload paths including dangling links, and unavailable fixed `/bin/sh` or `/bin/busybox`. Reserve one fresh `GUARD/native-shell` directory outside the root; preserve all probe/guard evidence. Use a dedicated synchronous launch subshell, with explicit exec into native env/chroot, clean allowlisted PATH/LC_ALL/HOME/TMPDIR, stdin detached and bounded fresh stdout/stderr captures. Close FD3–5/7–9 only in that child; preserve FD6 through chroot. The fixed inner shell script's first operation is `exec 6<&-`, followed by fixed native BusyBox checks/printf and exactly `CFMGR_NATIVE_SHELL_V1` plus LF. No background/pipeline/command-substitution launcher, arbitrary payload, inherited environment selectors or expansion of io.sh's capture command allowlist. Native ash's saved redirections above9 are closed by its external-exec path; explicit child closure alone is not proof of that boundary.

The probe returns0 only for exit0, exact sentinel bytes, empty stderr and verified fresh completion. A normally completed child status0..128 with a negative bounded response may yield1 only after validating captures/completion; malformed API returns2 before effects. After reservation any interrupted/abnormal producer, incomplete capture/preparation/observation/completion or early owner exit is129; propagate it unchanged through the callback so root teardown stays guarded. Root/Opt checks and ordinary non-lazy teardown remain the existing owner's responsibility. A successful probe establishes only this fixed native interpreter/BusyBox launch; it does not approve arbitrary ELF, NSS/TLS/config behavior, maintainer scripts or ordinary opkg.

[Configuration loading](https://github.com/openwrt/opkg-lede/blob/80503d94e356476250adaf1f669ee955ec26de76/libopkg/opkg_conf.c#L446) precedes creat/lockf acquisition at492–510; feeds/status/commands follow successful loading. [Install](https://github.com/openwrt/opkg-lede/blob/80503d94e356476250adaf1f669ee955ec26de76/libopkg/opkg_cmd.c#L467) unconditionally calls configure_packages(NULL) after selected attempts; lines397–423 iterate all unpacked packages. Separate configure NAME filtering, nodeps or download-only do not provide atomic unrelated-partial-state exclusion with ordinary install semantics. A status precheck releases its lock before install, and a CFMgr cooperative lock cannot exclude external opkg or configuration writers. Independently stable configuration and exclusion across admission/action therefore remain operational prerequisites. The upstream linked library could support a custom same-process consumer, but that is outside the selected installed-CLI policy and is not adopted. **O5 worker-lifetime design and proof gate:** matching Merlin433fc608f5fc1689f3d3c3ab5cd2a7d57102260f BusyBox miscutils/crond.c:775 calls `bb_setpgrp()` immediately before executing a job shell; the matched configuration enables CROND and disables its sendmail branch. This supplies a possible native process-group launch even though native setsid/timeout applets and shell job control are disabled. Operational admission must verify actual group leadership; hooks only queue bounded work. An in-group watchdog may signal its current group (`kill ... 0`), avoiding stored numeric PID/PGID reuse. Cancellation needs a cooperative done/ack transition, not killing a possibly reaped watcher PID. Persist uncertainty before group termination and count unresolved guards against admission; kernel uninterruptible IO cannot be promised to die by a userspace deadline.

Ordinary opkg can configure all unpacked packages and execute shell maintainer scripts, including detached descendants; direct opkg exit and group death do not prove those descendants finished. The candidate filesystem lifetime contract uses a private read-only root mount with read-only empty fallback /opt and /tmp, approved writable Entware and bounded private tmp child mounts, and inherited root directory-FD leases for every launcher before chroot entry. No launch authority may remain when teardown starts. Descendants retain an fs root reference even after setsid; ordinary non-lazy child/root unmounts can conservatively certify filesystem quiescence. Removing a child bind is write revocation, not harmless observation: any root still busy afterward is uncertain/guarded, never successful, even if direct opkg returned0. Root refs prove filesystem quiescence, not reaped descendants. This is a trusted-package compatibility boundary, not a hostile-root security sandbox or actual Merlin acceptance. No manual IPK resolver/offline-root mode is revived.

**O6 frozen native group-admission primitive:** source-only modules/worker.sh exposes `cfmgr_worker_group_check` with no arguments. This is a quiet, read-only check for the actual top-level shell process being its process-group leader, not authorization to signal, fork, launch opkg or clean resources. It must read the literal `/proc/self/stat` with shell builtins in the calling process, before any subshell/external reader, then validate observed PID equals the caller's `$$` and observed process-group ID equals that same PID. Native cron creates a group, not necessarily a session, so session ID need not match. Calling from an ordinary nested subshell must fail even though POSIX `$$` still denotes the outer shell. Return0 for the observation,1 for unavailable/malformed/not-leader state and2 for bad API. No PID is retained as later kill authority; future cancellation must signal the watchdog's current group after trusted launch/admission.

Preserve caller flags/traps/IFS/FDs; bounded kernel metadata may use a temporary function-scoped FD6, restored afterward. Read one newline-terminated record and require immediate EOF, rejecting embedded newlines/trailing records; validate a <=4096-byte record, canonical positive PID/group decimals, correct `(comm)` framing using the last closing delimiter and supported leading stat fields. Parse under fixed locale/IFS/noglob without evaluating data. No environment-selected proc path or new public test-path API is needed: cheap fixtures can exercise the internal record/parser or retained-reader helper; actual Linux production calls provide distinct evidence. Source and functions remain inert until explicitly called; caller tracing is already disabled.

**O5/O6 primary-source refinement:** the matching BusyBox include/platform.h:289–295 defines `bb_setpgrp()` as `setpgrp()` on Linux; cron does not check its return, so actual self-observation is mandatory. **O7 frozen deadline-controller contract (31–32%):** extend modules/worker.sh with internal `cfmgr_worker_deadline_with GUARD TOTAL_SECONDS GRACE_SECONDS CALLBACK [ARGS...]`. This entry is for one dedicated, trusted cron process group, with no foreign members and no subsequent unrelated work in that group. It is not a general shell timeout. Pure API validation precedes effects: canonical absolute guard path, total4..3600 seconds, grace1..30 strictly smaller than total, and trusted callback-name grammar. Require the original top-level shell to pass current-group admission and reject PID1. GUARD already denotes a trusted, exclusive, stable private RAM directory; reserve its fresh `deadline` child directory without replacing existing state. Return2 for malformed API and1 only for refusal before a watchdog starts. Retain the guard and every deadline marker on every outcome; a later lifecycle owner alone may remove them after all of its other completion gates.

Take one native `/proc/uptime` epoch before preparation that belongs to this action. Use canonical nonnegative uint31 whole seconds and elapsed subtraction, rejecting backward/unreadable/invalid clocks. The total budget includes setup, callback, cleanup and termination grace: stop accepting work/completion at elapsed TOTAL-GRACE, and escalate no later than elapsed TOTAL, subject to kernel/scheduler delays. Early cancellation may grant at most GRACE from that cancellation, capped by the same overall deadline. Fixed native one-second sleep polling is sufficient; do not add a 10Hz fork loop on firmware with disabled ash test/printf builtins. Native mkdir/sleep are fixed-path tools, not Entware or ambient PATH selections. The implementation may use `_cfmgr_worker_deadline_clock_now` as a quiet internal seconds producer so focused host tests can replace that function explicitly; production never selects a clock from environment/input.

Launch one watchdog only after reserving persistent uncertainty state. It observes its own actual proc record and requires PGRP to equal the admitted original leader, without requiring watchdog PID==leader. Before publishing `deadline/armed`, it establishes signal protection for HUP/INT/QUIT/TERM and validates the clock/tool setup. Only then may the controller invoke one trusted synchronous callback with unchanged arguments. The callback must include all its required cleanup and return status>128 when uncertain; this contract does not authorize arbitrary Entware children until the separate root-lifetime implementation exists. The watcher closes unrelated FD3..9 (no descriptors above9 are permitted at entry) and must not pin the execution root. It never launches into that root. Controller/callback state is isolated; ordinary successful return preserves caller flags/traps/IFS/FDs.

Use empty, fixed-name private directories `armed`, `done`, `ack`, `cancel` and `expired` under `deadline` for protocol publication; no parsing/eval or partially written status payload is needed. The controller publishes done only after a callback status0..128 and no observed interruption. The watcher validates done, takes a fresh clock sample before the cutoff, irreversibly disarms, publishes ack and exits; no later branch may signal. The controller requires an ordinary successful exact-child wait plus a valid ack and no sticky interruption before returning the callback status. Native mkdir exit failure, stopped/interrupted/failed wait, callback status>128, failed clock/sleep/publication or other post-launch uncertainty must never return ordinary success or leave a signal-capable watcher behind after a normal return.

Cancellation records best-effort cancel/expired intent while the already retained guard is sufficient uncertainty evidence, signals only the actor's current group0, protects the cancelling actor from group TERM/HUP/INT/QUIT, then uses current-group KILL within the remaining budget. The admitted controller may use the same cancellation path if its watchdog fails; neither actor changes its own process group after admission. Never signal a stored numeric PID/PGID. Post-launch uncertainty may terminate the entire dedicated group and therefore has no guaranteed shell return status. Kernel-uninterruptible work and externally stopped/killed supervisors cannot yield an unconditional hard-kill/reaping promise; retain guard/resources rather than claim completion. No cron/hook/CLI wiring, opkg, mount, root cleanup or router execution in O7.

O7 clock refinement: each actor rejects backward movement relative to its last accepted sample, not just the shared epoch. Poll loops also have a conservative finite iteration cap derived from the admitted budget, so a stuck valid-looking clock cannot cause an unbounded loop; exhausting the cap is uncertain cancellation. Elapsed differences avoid adding a budget to a near-limit uint31 timestamp.

O7 completion refinement: the owner may wait for ack within the overall TOTAL budget. The watcher's fresh-clock completion decision, callback/startup and done publication still require the earlier TOTAL-GRACE cutoff. This permits the reserved remainder to carry a valid completion handoff without treating polling latency alone as late callback work. Cancellation never adds another grace period beyond TOTAL; refresh the clock after TERM before deciding whether any grace sleep remains.

**Matched tmpfs source evidence:** kernel 4.1 `shmem.c` rounds requested size upward to page size; zero block or inode caps mean unlimited. Its mount-option report prints size in KiB with a `k` suffix and a decimal inode cap, omitting each when equal to the current default. It reports nondefault mode, including 0700. Therefore a successful mount command or requested option string alone is insufficient: require visible, matching effective positive caps, and conservatively refuse omitted or mismatched values rather than guessing defaults or page size. This does not reserve physical RAM or prove available-memory headroom. [Size/inode parsing](https://github.com/RMerl/asuswrt-merlin.ng/blob/433fc608f5fc1689f3d3c3ab5cd2a7d57102260f/release/src-rt-5.02axhnd/kernel/linux-4.1/mm/shmem.c#L2598-L2624) and [reported options](https://github.com/RMerl/asuswrt-merlin.ng/blob/433fc608f5fc1689f3d3c3ab5cd2a7d57102260f/release/src-rt-5.02axhnd/kernel/linux-4.1/mm/shmem.c#L2706-L2723) were checked directly by the parent; no router mount was performed.

**Native-device implementation design notes (not released):** keep fixed device policy and wrappers in a separate `modules/lib/native_devices.sh`, using explicit dependencies and a new literal composition selection. Existing native/Opt APIs remain unchanged. Create exactly two fresh 0600 character nodes beneath the private owned image after RAM/image admission, then retain their metadata and exact mount identity before building child views. Never open a source node merely to inspect it. A bounded native numeric `ls` observation plus `test -c`, non-symlink checks and inode equality can verify type, rdev, mode and identity; a small explicit character-record mode in the existing storage parser is preferable to another generic parser. Source observation must account for path spaces without parsing a variable filename as whitespace fields; changing to the private device directory and inspecting fixed literal names is a candidate. Preserve numeric inode identity as text. Exact parser shape, API and query budget must be frozen before delegation.

The cached matched BusyBox `coreutils/ls.c` prints `-i` inode values with a minimum seven-character decimal width, then mode, link count, numeric UID/GID, major/minor and date/name fields. A candidate `ls -dni null` / `ls -dni urandom` observation therefore has eleven fields and permits only leading space padding; preserve the inode decimal as text rather than converting it through awk floating point. Reusing the existing strict date/device grammar with a distinct literal character mode can keep old blockdev behavior unchanged. A metadata transaction may change into the private device directory only inside its isolated IO owner, which must finish and release its cwd before teardown. These are source-backed implementation notes, not a frozen parser or router capability proof.

Child views require private `ro,nosuid,noexec,dev` semantics: mountinfo normally expresses dev by absence of nodev, so do not require a literal dev token that the kernel need not emit. Pin each child to its owned image node and base-root parent; check all eight fixed children around the trusted observer. Cleanup remains Opt first, then the two device views and existing tmp/native/root teardown. Removing a device view exposes its original character node beneath the base root's nodev mount; the real-kernel consumer must witness refusal of new opens there, while preserving the distinction that existing device FDs may survive. No broad device directory bind, general device creation interface or production device IO probe. Reuse the existing ninth kernel scenario and one BusyBox representative, with cheap host metadata/option/identity faults. An additional source query before each bind and around the observer is justified only by its identity claim; derive the exact ceiling from the final sequence rather than choosing a convenient round number. No code/tests for this next package may start before the 37% gates close.

**F6 frozen completion contract:** audit only materialize→fetch/archive→hash/size. Internal results are 0 completed success, 10 deliberate completed failure, 2 invalid input without cleanup authority, and 129 uncertainty. At direct synchronous native boundaries ordinary nonzero becomes10 and any signal-like result greater than128 becomes129; nested shell/helper boundaries accept only their defined results, never normalize unexpected shell1/2 into completion. Single-producer subshells explicitly exec; substitutions check status before comparing output. Public materialize/fetch/archive APIs retain0/1/2 through normalization and cannot establish cleanup. New internal `_cfmgr_bootstrap_materialize_owned TOOLS PROFILE DIRECTORY` resets `_materialize_complete=0` then sets1 only for audited internal0/10, returning0/1 respectively; all other results retain completion0 and return129. Preserve the old closure-size consumer interface with a shared audited size body/entry; later closure build/hash/image errors remain F5-retained. Reset caught EXIT/HUP/INT/TERM traps only within audited subshell supervisors, preserving isolation-owner traps and the existing trust in synchronous native tools that leave no background descendants.

Isolation marks staging attempted before acquisition so completed failure still requires fresh private RAM/root identity before cleanup. Complete acquisition failure may clear prepare and return1; uncertainty retains it. Successful acquisition keeps prepare through all later image/root preparation. No disk terminal record, new polling loop, asynchronous launch, process search, signal sending, stale-guard recovery or aggregate-deadline claim. This is a narrow retry foundation, not final R35/R36 acceptance. [POSIX shell command status](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/utilities/V3_chap02.html) specifies signal termination above128; its possible larger values must be normalized before internal return. Saved native ash getstatus source additionally uses128+signal, but current CI and eventual Merlin acceptance remain distinct.

Native OpenSSL remains bootstrap/edge fallback; SHA256 package is required. Document kernel/ABI/feed boundaries and direct/transitive packages. P1.20/P2.7/V74. |
| R37 | A safe standalone health check with --diagnostic and --doctor aliases. | Both arguments run the same report without normal startup or dependency repair. Show available router model/firmware/kernel/userspace/tool context and stable PASS/FAIL/SKIP check IDs. Test actual runtime commands/options with synthetic bounded work; distinguish missing packages, unavailable Entware, broken tools, unsupported arguments and dependent skips. No config/service/provider/package mutations; private temporary probe files only. Redact secrets and sensitive identifiers. P2.8/V75. |

All three fully configured features also expose quick `cfmgr start <service>` / `cfmgr stop <service>` shortcuts through the same On/Off handlers, with strict configured/integrity gates, normalized case/aliases and truthful per-step notices as defined below. These are planned interfaces only.

## Porting audit and remaining edge cases

Review completed against the supplied source on 2026-10-08 from CFMgr base `5ceb412`; all six published fingerprints above still match. This is a source/specification audit, with no reference-script execution or live-router/provider test. The plan covers the main capabilities and intentionally extends them; the following mapping makes the porting obligations and remaining gaps explicit. Earlier inventory wording missed Python inside DDNS record enumeration and is corrected above.

**Runtime language boundary:** IP-Sync is a complete rewrite as BusyBox-compatible POSIX `sh`, using verified firmware tools, bundled shell/awk helpers and the selected Entware prerequisites in R36/D55. Preserve the reference's observable behavior and safeguards, not its Python implementation. Do not ship, invoke, wrap or fall back to `cloudflare-access-ip.py`, Python or a virtualenv on the router. DDNS record parsing and updater metadata parsing use the same verified shell/JSON facilities. Python/pytest is confined to developer/CI tests and excluded from the runtime package.
